rationale: From ⲥⲏϣⲉ 'be bitter.' Substantival use in gustatory register: 'fruit — the bitter.' Fits the Manichaean correspondential register where the dark spirits produce bitter fruit/taste.
Lyc ϯⲡⲉ = Sah. ϯⲡⲉ 'taste, kind, manner.' In a passage about fruit and bitterness, gustatory 'taste' is preferred over 'manner.'
Compound ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ϯ-ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('give a sign'). Designation for diviners/portent-interpreters in a list of practitioners through whom the dark spirit operates.
Possibly from ϣⲣ̄ⲡ 'first, before' = those who tell beforehand. Parallel to sign-givers and inquiring spirits in a divinatory list. Confidence low.

Greek-derived garment-term, possibly κωσθήνη or related. Context (paired with 'worship of bodies' and 'politeia') confirms a garment/vesture sense — what one wears as participation in the dark spirits' realm.

Greek loan πολιτεύεσθαι 'live as citizen, conduct one's life.' The infinitive substantivized with article ⲡ- becomes 'the conducting of citizenship/life-as-citizen' — i.e., one's whole mode of social-bodily existence.
Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- noun of unidentified root. Context places it parallel to 'garment' and 'politeia' — embodied participation in the realm of the five dark spirits. Tentative; awaiting parallels.
From ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, judge.' Paired with ⲕⲟⲗⲁⲥⲓⲥ 'punishment' in standard eschatological collocation.

Lyc form of ⲧⲱϩⲙ̄ 'summon, call, invite.' Functions as the technical verb of serial emanation in this kephalaion: the five Fathers were 'called forth one from another.' Repeated in line 26 of the Father's three further emanations.
Ordinal of ⲥⲁϣϥ/ⲥⲁϣϩ 'seven.' Lyc/scribal ϩ for ϥ. Used in chapter heading 'the Seventh: Concerning the Five Fathers.'
Standard Manichaean title for the second emanation of the Father of Greatness, identified here as the second of the Five Fathers. ⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ 'beloved' + ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'lights' (plural).
Title-pair: ⲡⲁⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'glorious one' (already in vocab) + ⲉⲧⲥⲙⲁⲙⲁⲁⲧ qualitative 'blessed.' Applied to the Father of Greatness.
